round-bottom-flask.context: A round glass flask with a straight neck and liquid filling the ball. Used for chemistry lab guides, reaction setups and science course material.

volumetric-flask.context: A pear-shaped flask with a very long thin neck, a single fill mark and a stopper. Used for preparing exact solutions in chemistry labs and lab-skills lessons.

side-arm-flask.context: A conical flask with a small hose barb sticking out of the neck. Used for vacuum filtration, filtering guides and lab equipment lists.

graduated-cylinder.context: A tall narrow measuring cylinder with a spout, a wide foot and tick marks. Used for measuring liquid volume in lab and school science content.

burette.context: A long graduated tube with a tap near the bottom and a drop falling from the tip. Used for titration, analytical chemistry and lab technique guides.

separatory-funnel.context: A pear-shaped glass funnel with a stopper on top, two liquid layers inside and a tap on the stem. Used for liquid extraction and separating immiscible liquids in chemistry.

buchner-funnel.context: A wide flat-topped funnel with a perforated plate, sitting in a collar on a flask neck. Used for vacuum filtration setups and lab equipment guides.

thistle-funnel.context: A long thin glass tube with a small bulb and a flared cup on top, like a thistle flower. Used for adding liquid to a sealed flask in gas experiments.

filter-funnel.context: A glass lab funnel holding a folded filter paper cone with a drop falling from the stem. Used for gravity filtration and separating solids from liquids.

watch-glass.context: A shallow curved glass dish seen from the side with a drop falling toward it. Used for holding small samples, evaporating tiny amounts and lab equipment lists.

evaporating-dish.context: A wide shallow bowl with a pouring lip and wisps of vapor rising from it. Used for boiling off solvent and heating solutions in chemistry labs.

crucible-tongs.context: Long scissor-like tongs gripping a small crucible cup at the tip. Used for handling hot crucibles and lab safety or equipment guides.

test-tube-holder.context: A spring clothespin-style clamp with a long handle gripping a test tube near its mouth. Used for heating test tubes safely and lab equipment guides.

reagent-bottle.context: A squat glass bottle with a mushroom stopper and a blank label. Used for storing chemicals in labs, stock rooms and chemistry teaching material.

dropper-bottle.context: A small bottle with a rubber bulb dropper cap and a blank label. Used for indicators, liquid reagents, eye drops style dosing and chemistry kits.

desiccator.context: A wide glass pot with a domed lid, a knob and a perforated plate across the middle. Used for keeping samples dry and chemistry equipment lists.

glass-condenser.context: A long diagonal tube inside a wider jacket with two small hose inlets on opposite sides. Used for distillation, reflux and organic chemistry lessons.

distillation-setup.context: A round flask over a flame joined by an angled condenser to a collecting flask. Used for distillation topics, separating liquids and chemistry teaching.

retort-stand.context: A heavy flat base with an upright rod and a clamp arm holding a small round flask. Used for supporting glassware in experiments and lab equipment guides.

bunsen-burner.context: An upright burner barrel on a round base with a side gas inlet and a pointed flame. Used for heating in school labs and chemistry safety content.

spirit-lamp.context: A squat glass jar with a wick holder in the lid and a small teardrop flame. Used for gentle heating in school labs and equipment lists.

tripod-gauze.context: A three-legged metal stand with a square wire mesh on top and a flame below. Used for heating beakers and flasks and lab equipment guides.

stirring-rod.context: A slim glass rod leaning in a beaker of liquid with a wavy surface. Used for mixing solutions, dissolving samples and chemistry lab skills.

lab-spatula.context: A thin metal spatula with a curved spoon end and a flat blade at the other end. Used for scooping and transferring powders and solids in labs.

rubber-stopper.context: A tapered rubber plug seen from the side with one hole through the middle. Used for sealing flasks and tubes and lab supply lists.

retort.context: A round glass vessel with a long neck that bends down and tapers to a point. Used for old-style distilling, alchemy themes and chemistry history.

vacuum-bell-jar.context: A glass dome with a knob sitting on a flat plate with a small bell hanging inside. Used for vacuum demonstrations and physics teaching.

chromatography-column.context: A vertical glass column with colored bands stacked inside and a tap at the bottom. Used for purifying and separating mixtures in chemistry.

paper-chromatography.context: A paper strip standing in a beaker of solvent with separated spots on it. Used for separating inks and pigments in school science.

sample-vial.context: A short cylindrical vial with a crimped cap and a septum dot on top. Used for sample storage, autosamplers and analytical lab content.

microcentrifuge-tube.context: A small conical tube with a snap cap hinged open to the side. Used for biology and molecular lab work, samples and equipment lists.

cuvette.context: A small square-sided transparent tube with a light beam passing through it. Used for spectrophotometry and measuring absorbance in labs.

volumetric-pipette.context: A long thin glass pipette with a bulge in the middle and a mark on the upper stem. Used for measuring a fixed liquid volume exactly in chemistry.

magnetic-stirrer.context: A flat plate with a dial under a beaker holding a stir bar and a swirl in the liquid. Used for mixing solutions in chemistry and biology labs.

orbital-shaker.context: A flat platform holding two flasks with a circular arrow showing the shaking motion. Used for culture growth, mixing and biology lab equipment lists.

lab-water-bath.context: A rectangular tank with two test tubes poking out of the lid and wavy heat lines inside. Used for warming samples at a steady temperature in labs.

fume-hood.context: A tall cabinet with a sash window raised halfway and an exhaust duct on top. Used for safe work with chemicals, lab safety and facility signs.

spectrophotometer.context: A benchtop instrument with a sample lid and a small display showing a graph peak. Used for measuring absorbance and concentration in labs.

rotary-evaporator.context: A round flask dipping into a heated bath, joined by an arm to a coiled condenser and motor. Used for removing solvent in organic chemistry labs.

electron-microscope.context: A tall column instrument made of stacked sections beside a monitor. Used for nanoscale imaging, materials science and research facilities.

microtome.context: A block machine with a hand wheel on the side and a blade slicing a thin curled ribbon. Used for cutting thin tissue sections in histology and pathology.

bioreactor.context: A stainless tank with a domed top, a motor, a stirrer shaft inside and pipes leading in. Used for fermentation, cell culture and biotech production.

chemistry-set.context: An open case holding two test tubes of liquid, like a beginner chemistry kit. Used for science toys, home experiments and educational products.

analytical-balance.context: A precision scale with a glass draft shield around the weighing pan and a display at the front. Used for weighing milligram amounts in labs.

beam-balance.context: A two-pan balance on a central post with a beam tilted so the left pan hangs lower. Used for comparing masses, physics lessons and fairness themes.

triple-beam-balance.context: A weighing pan on the left and three horizontal beams with sliding weights on the right. Used for school science mass measurement.

spring-scale.context: A hanging tube scale with tick marks, a hook at the bottom and a weight pulling it down. Used for measuring force and weight in physics.

calibration-weight.context: A stubby metal test weight with a knob on top and a smaller one beside it. Used for checking scale accuracy, metrology and lab equipment lists.

chemical-reaction.context: Two small particles with an arrow pointing to one larger combined particle. Used for chemistry topics, reaction types and lesson material.

reversible-reaction.context: Two half-headed arrows stacked and pointing in opposite directions, the sign for chemical equilibrium. Used in chemistry equations and teaching.

covalent-bond.context: Two overlapping atoms sharing a pair of electrons in the lens where they meet. Used for chemical bonding lessons and molecule topics.

ionic-bond.context: A small positive ion touching a larger negative ion, each marked with its charge sign. Used for bonding lessons, salts and electrostatics.

hydrogen-bond.context: Two water molecules with a dotted link between a hydrogen of one and the oxygen of the other. Used for water properties and intermolecular forces.

crystal-lattice.context: A cube of atoms joined by rods in a repeating three-dimensional grid. Used for solid state chemistry, minerals and materials science.

water-molecule.context: One large oxygen ball with two small hydrogen balls attached at an angle, like a mouse head. Used for water, h2o and chemistry topics.

carbon-dioxide-molecule.context: Three touching balls in a line, a carbon between two oxygens. Used for co2, climate, carbon emissions and chemistry topics.

methane-molecule.context: A central carbon ball with four small hydrogen balls on sticks spread in a tetrahedron. Used for ch4, natural gas and organic chemistry topics.

buckyball.context: A round cage of hexagons and pentagons like a soccer ball, built around a central pentagon. Used for fullerene, c60 and nanotechnology topics.

graphene-sheet.context: A patch of honeycomb made of joined carbon hexagons. Used for graphene, 2d materials, nanotechnology and carbon chemistry.

carbon-nanotube.context: A slanted open tube whose wall is a mesh of hexagons. Used for nanotechnology, carbon materials and advanced materials topics.

polymer-chain.context: A zigzag chain of linked beads with a bracket over the repeating unit. Used for polymer chemistry, plastics and macromolecule topics.

protein-structure.context: A coiled ribbon helix flowing into a flat arrow-shaped sheet. Used for protein folding, biochemistry and molecular biology topics.

lipid-bilayer.context: Two rows of round heads with tails pointing toward each other, like a cell membrane. Used for membrane biology and biochemistry topics.

enzyme.context: A round protein with a wedge-shaped notch and a small wedge-shaped molecule fitting toward it. Used for lock and key, catalysts and metabolism topics.

states-of-matter.context: Three bands of dots: tightly packed, loosely spaced and widely scattered. Used for solid, liquid and gas lessons and particle theory.

filtration.context: A funnel over a flask with a drop falling from the stem. Used for separating solids from liquids, water treatment and lab technique.

evaporation.context: A water surface with three wavy vapor lines rising and ending in arrowheads. Used for the water cycle, drying and phase change topics.

condensation.context: A cold glass beaded with water droplets, one of them running down. Used for the water cycle, humidity and phase change topics.

electrolysis.context: A beaker with two electrodes wired to a battery and bubbles rising from each. Used for splitting water, electroplating and electrochemistry.

voltaic-pile.context: A stack of flat metal discs with a wire leaving the top disc on one side and the bottom disc on the other. Used for early batteries and electricity history.

lemon-battery.context: A lemon with two wires pushed into it and a small light bulb above. Used for fruit battery experiments, school electricity projects and stem.

element-tile.context: A square periodic table tile with a large letter symbol, a small number in the corner and a bar for the mass. Used for chemistry and periodic table content.

chirality.context: Two mirror-image molecules with different attachments, facing each other across a dashed line. Used for handedness, enantiomers and stereochemistry.

fire-triangle.context: A triangle with a flame in the middle, the model of heat, fuel and oxygen needed for a fire. Used for fire safety and combustion lessons.

flame-test.context: A wire loop holding a sample in a flame above a burner barrel. Used for identifying metal ions by flame color in school chemistry.

litmus-paper.context: A thin paper test strip with a darker dipped end, beside a drop of liquid. Used for testing acids and bases in school chemistry and pool or soil tests.

ph-scale.context: A horizontal color bar with dividers and a pointer above the neutral middle. Used for acid and base lessons, water quality and cleaning products.

ph-meter.context: A handheld meter with a small display and buttons, its probe on a cord dipped in a beaker. Used for measuring acidity of water, soil and solutions.

precipitate.context: A test tube of liquid with a layer of grains settled at the bottom and specks still falling. Used for chemical tests and solubility lessons.

effervescence.context: A beaker of fizzing liquid with bubbles rising inside and bursting above the rim. Used for gas-releasing reactions, fizzy drinks and chemistry demos.
